response.rationale: Biopsy shows coagulative necrosis with karyorrhexis, characteristic of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease; other candidates lack this necrotizing pattern.

rejected.why: Sarcoidosis typically shows non-caseating granulomas, not coagulative necrosis; normal labs and negative mycobacteria argue against.
Rosai-Dorfman disease features sinus histiocytosis with emperipolesis, not coagulative necrosis with karyorrhexis.
Castleman disease may have lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate but lacks the necrotizing karyorrhectic pattern seen here.
